factors.label: Car, Taxi, Tempo, Auto Rickshaw & Pick up
Tractor Trailor, Truck Trailor Units (3 Axle & MAV)

survey_design: 11 May 2026 is a Monday; the methodology specifies Tue/Wed/Thu and excludes Monday.
May is pre-monsoon peak heat; recommended windows are Oct-Nov or Feb-Mar.
No weekend day surveyed; the stated minimum is three days including Sat and Sun.
U-turns were never counted. Twelve movements per junction, not sixteen.

assumptions.capacity_source: IRC:92-2017 Table 6.3 / Indo-HCM Table 5.4, four-lane divided urban

capacity.width_caveat: A transect cannot distinguish a through lane from a service road. Ten transects measure over 14 m per direction, up to 19.8 m, which is five running lanes each way. That is possible on this corridor and it is also what a service road looks like from above. Capacity scales linearly with this, so treat the northern junctions as an upper bound until the carriageway is confirmed on site.

assumptions.conflicting_stream: opposing through movement at the U-turn bay

scheme.gap_source: composition-weighted from literature; benchmarked against IRC:SP:41-1994 Appendix III Table III-2 passenger-car value and Indo-HCM 2017 base gaps
scheme.uturn_analogue: merge into the opposing stream, not a crossing of it
scheme.feeds_bay: right turns from all four arms, plus the cross-street through movement
scheme.gap_direction_note: our gap sits mid-pack in the Indian field evidence - above the Kerala openings, below Gupta, CSIR-CRRI and IRC:SP:41 - so the finding rests on neither the generous nor the punitive end
scheme.two_wheeler_gap_basis: Gupta, Mondal & Sharma 2018 (Varanasi, four-lane divided, 7.03-8.90 m per direction) 3.83 s and Datta & Bhuyan 2014 (six four-lane median openings) 3.37-4.78 s; 3.5 s sits inside both

gap_evidence_spread.label: Kerala median openings, traditional/Raff
gap_evidence_spread.source: Kumar & Sasikumar 2020, IJTTE 10(4), six mid-block median openings, Kerala
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: median openings, but the paper states carriageway width only and never lane count - reading it as four-lane was our inference, not theirs

gap_evidence_spread.label: Kerala median openings, merging behaviour
gap_evidence_spread.source: Kumar & Sasikumar 2020; merging behaviour is the method those authors recommend for mixed traffic
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: median openings, lane count not stated in the paper

gap_evidence_spread.label: Khan 2022 thesis, four-lane median openings, modified Raff / binary logit
gap_evidence_spread.source: T. Khan PhD thesis 2022, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, ch. 7-8; the dataset behind Khan et al. TRR 2678 and 2679, which are closed access. Values may differ from the edited papers
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: closest of all: four-lane divided median openings, and the only source with a MEASURED four-lane follow-up time (2.04 s, two-wheelers, Table 8.2)

gap_evidence_spread.label: Mohan & Chandra 2020, RT from minor, 4-lane divided
gap_evidence_spread.source: Can. J. Civ. Eng. 47(6), produced under the CSIR-CRRI Indo-HCM project
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: four-lane divided major, but a junction movement not a median opening

gap_evidence_spread.label: Datta & Bhuyan 2014, four-lane median openings, prob. equilibrium
gap_evidence_spread.source: Datta & Bhuyan 2014, ICAET, six median openings on four-lane divided roads, Odisha and Jharkhand; mean over all classes and sites
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: closest by road type: median openings explicitly on four-lane divided

gap_evidence_spread.label: Khan 2022 thesis, four-lane median openings, occupancy time / SVM
gap_evidence_spread.source: same thesis; the authors conclude occupancy time and SVM give the values closest to published literature, so this is their own preferred pair
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: closest of all: four-lane divided median openings, authors' preferred methods

gap_evidence_spread.label: Gupta et al. 2018, four-lane median openings, Varanasi
gap_evidence_spread.source: Gupta, Mondal & Sharma 2018, Curr. Sci. 114(7) Table 5, traditional and INAFOGA over 30 observations; follow-up from Ramireddy et al. 2025 Siegloch measurement
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: closest overall: four-lane divided median openings, carriageway 7.03-8.90 m per direction against this corridor's ~7 m

gap_evidence_spread.label: CSIR-CRRI NH-8 design recommendation
gap_evidence_spread.source: Khan, Chalumuri & Senapathi 2015, J. EASTS 11:1842-1855; 748 U-turning vehicles across seven methods spanning 2.10-7.26 s; follow-up at the 0.6 x t_c convention
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: the only Indian DESIGN value for a median opening, but inter-urban NH not urban

gap_evidence_spread.label: Datta & Bhuyan 2014, four-lane median openings, INAFOGA
gap_evidence_spread.source: Datta & Bhuyan 2014; INAFOGA/merging-behaviour method, mean over all classes
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: closest by road type: median openings explicitly on four-lane divided

gap_evidence_spread.label: IRC:SP:41 Table III-2, RT from major, 4-lane, 48 kmph
gap_evidence_spread.source: IRC:SP:41-1994 Appendix III Table III-2, passenger cars, large-city adjustment applied
gap_evidence_spread.geometric_match: four-lane, but HCM 1985 in metric with no Indian calibration

scheme.indo_hcm_gap_source: Mohan & Chandra 2020, Can. J. Civ. Eng. 47(6), produced under the CSIR-CRRI Indo-HCM project: base critical gap, four-lane divided, right turn minor-to-major, via a secondary reproduction
scheme.indo_hcm_form_differs: Indo-HCM adds geometric factors a and b to the HCM form; we use a = 1, b = 0 because their values sit in a chapter no free copy of the manual reproduces
scheme.indo_hcm_no_uturn_chapter: Indo-HCM 2017 has no chapter, table or parameter set for mid-block median openings or U-turns; Annexure 7C is scoped to roundabouts. No Indian code publishes a design gap for the manoeuvre this scheme is built on.
scheme.csir_crri_design_source: Khan, Chalumuri & Senapathi 2015, J. EASTS 11:1842-1855, CSIR-CRRI, NH-8 Delhi-Manesar, 748 U-turning vehicles

sensitivity.growth_handled_in: swept interactively by the dashboard scenario tool and used for design life in capacity.py; it does not bear on the three conclusions tested here, so none of their grids sweep it

assumptions.vot_status: policy input - indicative, replace with JDA rates
assumptions.queue_carryover: not modelled - each oversaturated hour treated independently, so the figure is a lower bound

safety.caveat: exposure, not crash prediction; no accident data exists for this corridor

unverified: IRC:SP:84 clause 2.14 read from the 2014 edition; a 2019 edition exists and was not checked
IRC:103 zebra ceiling is from a revision draft, not the published 2022 edition, whose scan has no text layer
the 50% turning claim is news reporting, not a JDA document

omitted.time_space: bandwidth is time inside a green phase; this corridor is being made signal-free, so there is nothing to read
omitted.speed_flow: a classified count contains no speed or density; a fitted fundamental diagram would be decoration with axes
